question: Up to what order value can a purchase executive approve on their own, and who approves above that?
reference: A purchase executive may approve orders up to £250,000 gross, including VAT. Above that the order goes to the purchase manager, whose limit is £1,000,000.
contexts: [POL-PUR-001 §5.2] 5. Approval limits: 5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.

[POL-APR-002 §5.1] 5. Examples: 5.1 Emma Clarke (purchase executive) raises an order for 2,000 battery packs at £119.00: basic £238,000, VAT 20% £47,600, gross £285,600. The gross is above her £250,000 limit, so the order goes to her manager, Daniel Okafor (purchase manager, limit £1,000,000), for approval.
[POL-APR-002 §1] 1. Purpose: This matrix sets who may approve a purchase request or purchase order, and up to what value. It is the matrix referred to in Purchase Policy §5.2.
[POL-PUR-001 §5.4] 5. Approval limits: 5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's limit covers the order's gross value.
answer: A purchase executive's limit is £250,000, as shown in the example of Emma Clarke, and the comparison is against the gross order value [POL-APR-002 §5.1]. An order above that goes to the next person up whose limit covers it, which in the example is purchase manager Daniel Okafor, with a £1,000,000 limit [POL-PUR-001 §5.2; POL-APR-002 §5.1].

question: Can we order battery packs from a supplier that has no UN 38.3 certificate on file?
reference: No. Lithium-cell parts such as battery packs, hub motors and chargers may only be ordered from a supplier with a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file before the first order.
contexts: [POL-PUR-001 §6.2] 6. Supplier qualification: 6.2 **Lithium-cell parts** (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a **valid UN 38.3 certificate** on file in Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked **before the first order** is placed. An expired certificate counts as no certificate.

[POL-SUP-003 §4.1] 4. UN 38.3 certificates: 4.1 A supplier of any lithium-cell part (battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any item marked lithium-cell in the item master) must hold a UN 38.3 certificate. This is the certificate referred to in Purchase Policy §6.2.

[POL-SUP-003 §4.5] 4. UN 38.3 certificates: 4.5 An expired certificate counts as no certificate. The supplier stays ACTIVE in the master, but no lithium-cell part may be ordered from it until a new certificate is uploaded and checked.

[POL-SUP-003 §4.7] 4. UN 38.3 certificates: 4.7 Ledgerline does not stop an order to a supplier without a certificate. The check in this section is done by the person raising the order, and by the approver.
answer: No. Battery packs are lithium-cell parts, and these may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in Ledgerline [POL-PUR-001 §6.2]. Ledgerline won't block such an order, so the person raising it and the approver must perform the check [POL-SUP-003 §4.7].

question: What happens to an order that is charged to a closed cost centre?
reference: Ledgerline does not refuse it. The order is saved as Draft with warning W-CC-114 and nothing is sent to anyone.
contexts: [MAN-PUR-72 §8.1] 8. Cost centres (FIN-CC-01) › 8.1 Purpose: Every request and order is charged to a cost centre. The cost centre screen shows each cost centre's name, owner, status (OPEN or CLOSED) and the date it was closed, with its budget for the quarter and the amount already committed.

[MAN-PUR-72 §11.9] 11. Purchase order entry (PUR-PO-01) › 11.9 The status after saving: If the cost centre is closed, the order is saved as DR (Draft) with warning W-CC-114, and nothing is sent to anyone. If the gross value is within your limit, the order is AP (approved). If the order is against a request whose approver's limit covers the order's gross value, it is AP and the request's approver is recorded. Otherwise the order is PA and goes to the approver's inbox.

[MAN-PUR-72 §8.2] 8. Cost centres (FIN-CC-01) › 8.2 Status: Finance opens and closes cost centres. A closed cost centre cannot carry new spend. Ledgerline does not refuse a document charged to a closed cost centre: it saves the document as Draft and sets warning W-CC-114 (see §17.6).

[POL-PUR-001 §4.2] 4. Cost centres and budgets: 4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent to the supplier.
answer: An order charged to a closed cost centre is saved as a Draft with warning W-CC-114, and nothing is sent to anyone [MAN-PUR-72 §11.9]. A closed cost centre cannot carry new spend, and Ledgerline does not refuse the document but sets warning W-CC-114 [MAN-PUR-72 §8.2]. A Draft order is never sent to the supplier [POL-PUR-001 §4.2].

question: How recent must a supplier's UN 38.3 certificate be?
reference: Under amendment AMD-SUP-2026-02 the certificate must have been issued within the last 12 months and be valid for at least 60 days after the order date. This replaces the earlier 24-month rule.
contexts:
[AMD-SUP-2026-02 §1.1] 1. What changes: 1.1 With effect from 1 September 2026, Supplier Policy POL-SUP-003 §4.4 is replaced by the following:
"A UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if it was issued within the last 12 months, and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the order is placed."

[POL-SUP-003 §4.1] 4. UN 38.3 certificates: 4.1 A supplier of any lithium-cell part (battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any item marked lithium-cell in the item master) must hold a UN 38.3 certificate. This is the certificate referred to in Purchase Policy §6.2.

[POL-SUP-003 §4.6] 4. UN 38.3 certificates: 4.6 The certificate covers the supplier, not a single item. If the supplier changes the cells or the design of a part (for example a new cell maker or cell chemistry), it must give a fresh test report for that part.

[POL-SUP-003 §4.2] 4. UN 38.3 certificates: 4.2 The certificate must be a test report from a laboratory accredited for lithium-cell materials (for example a laboratory accredited to ISO/IEC 17025 for UN 38.3 testing).
answer: A UN 38.3 certificate must have been issued within the last 12 months, and its valid-to date must be at least 60 days after the order is placed [AMD-SUP-2026-02 §1.1]. This rule takes effect on 1 September 2026 and replaces POL-SUP-003 §4.4 [AMD-SUP-2026-02 §1.1].
